citation.claim: Primary map teaching can connect real places, photographs and plans, then develop direction, symbols, keys and purposeful map making.
citation.source: Royal Geographical Society, Map skills, primary lesson overviews Years 1–6.

maps.checked: 2026-11-18; Read lesson overviews, not all downloadable files. This supports the proposed sequence, not measured effectiveness of the authored tasks. Four-figure references in the source are distinct from the topic’s letter-number cell references.

citation.claim: Primary mapping guidance connects place, space and scale with enquiry, varied map sources, field observation and representations of change/connections.
citation.source: Paula Owens / Ordnance Survey (2021), Teaching map skills to primary children, especially pp. 13–15 and 30–35.

owens.checked: 2026-11-18; Read guidance, progression and enquiry examples. England-specific curriculum context is not a universal age ladder or evidence that these exact activities are validated.

citation.claim: Primary geography guidance recommends questions, collection/evaluation of varied evidence and mapped locality studies.
citation.source: Royal Geographical Society, Starting to Plan Primary Geography, enquiry and locality-study discussion.

enquiry.checked: 2026-11-18; Read substantive guidance. Do not turn suggested frequency or England-specific statutory statements into requirements elsewhere.

citation.claim: Primary pupils can distinguish natural, managed and built features using photographs, local observation, descriptive language and maps.
citation.source: NSW Department of Education, Field of Mars EEC, Features of places learning resource, lesson overviews.

features.checked: 2026-11-18; Read lessons 1–3 overview. Detailed child task designs here are authored adaptations, not imported lesson text or empirical misconception findings.

citation.claim: The AIATSIS map depicts general locations of language/social/nation groups; boundaries are not exact/fixed and the map is unsuitable for land claims.
citation.source: AIATSIS, Map of Indigenous Australia, description and limitations.

mapCountry.checked: 2026-11-18; Read map description, spelling variation and Country link. Do not reproduce the copyrighted map, infer an exact school identity from it, or equate its areas with state borders.

citation.claim: Acknowledgement recognises Traditional Owners and continuing connection to Country; anyone may offer it, while Welcome follows Traditional Owner authority/protocols.
citation.source: Reconciliation Australia, Acknowledgement of Country and Welcome to Country.

acknowledgement.checked: 2026-11-18; Read distinctions, Country meaning and consultation guidance. No generic page verifies the Country of a particular school. No template is reproduced.

citation.claim: Resource selection should examine First Nations participation, positioning, authority and production, respecting self-determination and cultural knowledge.
citation.source: AIATSIS (2022), Guide to evaluating and selecting education resources, Resource Evaluation Framework.

protocols.checked: 2026-11-18; Read framework and evaluative questions, PDF pp. 7–13. Original summaries only; this is professional guidance, not local endorsement of these proposed exercises.

citation.claim: Seasonal knowledge is place-specific and connected with caring for Country; published calendars retain their owners’ Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property and use conditions.
citation.source: CSIRO and Indigenous partners, Indigenous seasonal calendars, overview and ICIP conditions.

calendars.checked: 2026-11-18; Read overview and rights/permission sections. No calendar, artwork, language list or restricted knowledge is copied into this contribution. Teachers must check the relevant owner’s conditions before use.

citation.claim: Tiwi Traditional Owners and the Tiwi Land Council co-developed calendars connecting weather, plants/animals and seasonal knowledge.
citation.source: Tiwi Traditional Owners / Tiwi Land Council with CSIRO, Tiwi seasons and plants and animals calendars.

tiwi.checked: 2026-11-18; Read public collaboration description and seasonal overview. Download conditions were inspected but no download consent or reproduction permission is claimed. Use only authorised classroom resources; no Tiwi words/calendar content is reproduced.

citation.claim: Torres Strait Traditional Owners, rangers and scientists work together on seagrass monitoring and turtle conservation with communities.
citation.source: Torres Strait Regional Authority, Best of both worlds: Caring for land and sea with traditional knowledge and science.

rangers.checked: 2026-11-18; Read named practitioner account and work descriptions. Treat dated staffing totals as historical; no totals are taught. Do not make the Torres Strait case a universal account of all First Nations or a substitute for local knowledge.

citation.claim: Torres Strait community-based plans combine traditional use and contemporary science for culturally appropriate dugong/turtle management.
citation.source: Torres Strait Regional Authority, Dugong and Turtle Management Project, overview.

seaManagement.checked: 2026-11-18; Read project overview only. Not an authorisation to harvest wildlife or a claim that all places/species share one rule.

citation.claim: Gunditjmara engineered channels, weirs and dams at Budj Bim to manage water and trap/store/harvest kooyang, within continuing connections to Country.
citation.source: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape, World Heritage listing, overview and continuing cultural landscape.

budjbim.checked: 2026-11-18; Read landscape, hydrological management and cultural-continuity account. Cite the named people/place, not a generic ancient-only culture. No site plans or cultural designs reproduced.

citation.claim: Cultural fire is Aboriginal-led, connected to living culture and Country, and distinct from hazard reduction even where fuel-reduction benefits occur.
citation.source: NSW NPWS, Cultural fire policy, principles and sections 1–9.

culturalFire.checked: 2026-11-18; Read substantive principles and purpose/ICIP sections. This is NSW policy context, not a universal legal account. No practical burning activity or operating instructions are proposed.

citation.claim: Farm-animal welfare includes suitable nutrition/water, shelter, health care, behaviour and freedom from distress.
citation.source: RSPCA Australia Knowledgebase, What are the Five Freedoms of animal welfare?

welfare.checked: 2026-11-18; Read five freedoms and five-domains discussion. Classroom cases are conceptual; no child husbandry/veterinary performance certification or guaranteed welfare claim from one visible sign.

citation.claim: Wool is processed from shorn fleece through cleaning/preparation and spinning into yarn, then fabric production.
citation.source: Amgueddfa Cymru / National Wool Museum, The Process — from fleece to fabric.

wool.checked: 2026-11-18; Read sequence and stages. Historical mill details are not universal modern methods; historical chemical practices and machinery are not classroom activities. Knitting is a possible yarn-to-garment route, not the only one.

citation.claim: Cotton plants yield fibre; ginning separates lint from seed and spinning produces yarn before knitting/weaving and garment making.
citation.source: Cotton Australia, From Field to Fashion, Cotton Classroom senior poster.

cotton.checked: 2026-11-18; Read technical process descriptions. Simplify stage names without implying children operate equipment. Do not adopt the poster’s promotional blanket sustainability claims.

citation.claim: Aquaculture involves breeding/rearing/harvesting aquatic organisms in water environments, unlike capture alone.
citation.source: US NOAA National Ocean Service, What is aquaculture?

aquaculture.checked: 2026-11-18; Read definitions and examples. Distinguish farming from wild capture without claiming aquaculture must always use indoor tanks.

citation.claim: Protected cropping uses structures to modify growing conditions or protect crops from pests, disease and adverse weather.
citation.source: NSW DPIRD, Protected cropping, definition and overview.

protected.checked: 2026-11-18; Read substantive overview. Structures vary; a greenhouse does not automatically or perfectly control every variable. No practical pesticide or electrical setup proposed.

citation.claim: Greenhouse drain-water recycling can reduce water/fertiliser losses but requires suitable infrastructure, monitoring and disease-risk management.
citation.source: NSW DPIRD, Greenhouse drain water recycling in protected cropping — the rewards and the realities.

recycling.checked: 2026-11-18; Read benefits and constraints sections. No fixed percentage improvement or claim that recycling always works is inferred; professional procedures are not pupil instructions.

citation.claim: Murray–Darling water supports communities, farming and ecosystems; environmental water supports native vegetation, fish and waterbirds.
citation.source: DCCEEW / Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder, 2026–27 Water Management Plan, Executive Summary and Overview.

basin.checked: 2026-11-18; Read Basin importance and ecosystem planning sections. No fluctuating statistics are used as mastery facts or current local allocation promises.

citation.claim: Mangrove roots provide habitat/shelter for fish and other organisms; mangroves can protect coasts and support food webs.
citation.source: US NOAA National Ocean Service, What is a mangrove forest?

mangroves.checked: 2026-11-18; Read full explanatory page. Benefits depend on place; do not claim every native species uses mangroves or that vegetation prevents all flood/storm damage.

citation.claim: Mangrove ecosystems provide food/livelihood and wildlife benefits, linking vegetation and coastal communities.
citation.source: FAO, Mangrove Management: Ecosystem services.

mangroveUse.checked: 2026-11-18; Read ecosystem-service descriptions. Use separately located Australian and other-continent cases with attributed evidence, not one global stereotype.

citation.claim: Bushfire risk management involves authorities, land managers and communities, with planning and hazard-reduction activities.
citation.source: NSW Rural Fire Service, Bush Fire Risk Management Plans, introductory description.

fireRisk.checked: 2026-11-18; Read management-plan purpose, actors and possible works. No local plan documents, current incident details or real-time safe route have been verified.

citation.claim: Fire danger ratings support preparation and decisions under a bushfire plan; official local information should guide action.
citation.source: NSW Government, Fire danger ratings.

fireRatings.checked: 2026-11-18; Read explanation and rating/action sections. Child activity uses adult-prepared non-emergency examples, not independent safety decisions or a prediction that ignition is certain.

citation.claim: Levees can contain/control/divert water and reduce flood risk but do not prevent every flood.
citation.source: NSW State Emergency Service, Levees.

levees.checked: 2026-11-18; Read definition and limitations. Do not build/test a real barrier, enter floodwater or infer a real property is safe.

citation.claim: Drought management can prioritise critical human water needs and involve local utilities managing supplies and restrictions.
citation.source: NSW Government Water, Drought, floods and extreme events, drought-management section.

drought.checked: 2026-11-18; Read management context. Do not adopt the page’s broad drought-frequency shorthand or teach its regulatory priorities as universal outside NSW.

citation.claim: Water restrictions manage demand during scarcity, and their rules/responsible authorities vary locally.
citation.source: Bureau of Meteorology, Water Restrictions FAQs.

restrictions.checked: 2026-11-18; Read FAQ definition and local variation. No current restriction level is asserted for any place.

citation.claim: Australia’s six states and the ACT/NT have the eight named capitals; Canberra is also the national capital.
citation.source: Australian Department of Home Affairs, Our Common Bond, podcast episode 2 transcript, states and territories.

capitals.checked: 2026-11-18; Read capital list. The page’s “two mainland territories” is shorthand; other territories exist. Do not adopt the stale largest-city claim or total-territory implication.

citation.claim: Australia administers territories beyond the ACT and NT, including Jervis Bay, Norfolk Island, Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands.
citation.source: Australian Department of Infrastructure, Territories & regions, territories overview.

territories.checked: 2026-11-18; Read current territory list. Jervis Bay is not an external territory. Antarctic sovereignty/status is not generalised from a small school map.

citation.claim: A primary geography worksheet asks learners to locate and circle named Indo-Pacific neighbouring countries on a regional map.
citation.source: Australian DFAT, Our Indo-Pacific community, Years 3–4 worksheet, page 1.

neighbours.checked: 2026-11-18; Fetched the PDF and read page 1’s country table and locate/circle task. Its broad regional “nearest neighbours” list does not establish a precise nearest-distance ranking; choose named endpoints and an appropriate scale/tool. The map is not reproduced or used to certify the accuracy of a teacher-selected atlas.

citation.claim: Australia and Southeast Asia have migration, education and tourism connections alongside development cooperation.
citation.source: Australian DFAT, ASEAN and Australia, people connections and development sections.

connections.checked: 2026-11-18; Read substantive sections. No current spending/enrolment total or policy promise is treated as permanent knowledge. Classroom consequence cases are labelled hypothetical.

citation.claim: Census evidence distinguishes country of birth, ancestry, language and other dimensions rather than treating culture as a single fixed category.
citation.source: Australian Bureau of Statistics (2022), Cultural diversity of Australia, 2021 Census analysis.

diversity.checked: 2026-11-18; Read dated analysis and variable distinctions. Not a claim about any child’s background or proof one photograph represents a whole country. No personal migration histories are collected.

citation.claim: Singapore has a near-equatorial tropical climate with abundant rainfall and relatively small seasonal temperature variation.
citation.source: Meteorological Service Singapore, Climate of Singapore.

singapore.checked: 2026-11-18; Read climate/season descriptions. Site climate is not every Asian place, and weather on a particular day is not a climate normal.

citation.claim: The Melbourne Olympic Park table reports monthly temperature and rainfall summaries with stated observation periods.
citation.source: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Melbourne (Olympic Park) climate statistics, station 086338.

melbourne.checked: 2026-11-18; Read monthly table and period labels. Snapshot varies over time; classroom packs must preserve station, variable, units and years. Short station summaries are not automatically 30-year standard normals; compare matched measures cautiously.

citation.claim: NASA’s Earth-observation account shows the Himalaya, Tibetan Plateau and Indo-Gangetic plain as contrasting landforms.
citation.source: NASA Earth Observatory, Himalayas, Near and Far.

himalayas.checked: 2026-11-18; Read observation account; images are evidence of particular locations/dates, not all of Asia or a direct climate measure.

citation.claim: NASA’s April 2024 account locates the Gobi dust source in Inner Mongolia and tracks dust moving across East Asia.
citation.source: NASA Earth Observatory (26 April 2024), A Wall of Dust Over the Korean Peninsula.

gobi.checked: 2026-11-18; Read dated MODIS observation and source-location description. Replaces an inaccessible MODIS caption; no present forecast or claim that all Asian environments are desert. Only benign landscape comparisons are used in child tasks.

citation.claim: Great Artesian Basin groundwater supports pastoral/agricultural uses, town supplies, cultural values and groundwater-dependent ecosystems including springs.
citation.source: Geoscience Australia, Great Artesian Basin, resource and ecosystem overview.

artesian.checked: 2026-11-18; Read resource and groundwater-dependent ecosystem discussion. Do not teach a basin as an empty underground lake, all springs as uniform, or an annual economic figure as permanent knowledge.

citation.claim: The 2019–20 Black Summer bushfires had major consequences for NSW communities, farmers, businesses, wildlife and bushland.
citation.source: Australian Institute for Disaster Resilience, Black Summer bushfires, NSW, 2019–20, event summary.

blackSummer.checked: 2026-11-18; Read dated event impact summary. Use a brief non-graphic teacher account; do not assess distressing casualty statistics or infer present emergency advice.

citation.claim: Place teaching should examine prior views and source selection; any photograph offers only a selected view rather than a whole place or country.
citation.source: Geographical Association, Teaching distant places, resource selection and misrepresentation guidance.

comparison.checked: 2026-11-18; Read actual guidance on prior understanding, context and image selection. Secondary teacher-education context; primary exercises are adaptations and no exact child misconception prevalence or intervention effect is inferred.
